Thought: When combustible or flammable materials are mixed with oxidizing acids, several hazardous reactions can occur. Oxidizing acids (like nitric acid, perchloric acid, etc.) can provide oxygen to support or accelerate combustion. When these come in contact with flammable materials, they can cause:

1. Fire (B) - The oxidizing acid can cause ignition of the flammable material
2. Explosion (A) - Rapid oxidation reactions can lead to explosive conditions
3. Heat generation (D) - Exothermic reactions occur when oxidizers react with flammable materials
4. Toxic gas generation (H) - Some reactions may produce toxic gases

I don't see evidence for options like "Innocuous gas generation" or "Violent polymerization" being primary concerns in this specific combination.
